content_voiceover: This is the primary endpoint of QuANTUM-First, overall survival in the intention to treat population. The quizartinib arm, 268 patients, had a median overall survival of 31.9 months, versus 15.1 months with placebo plus standard chemotherapy in 271 patients. That's a 16.8 month improvement in median OS. The hazard ratio was 0.78, 95 percent confidence interval 0.62 to 0.98, p equals 0.032, so a statistically significant and clinically meaningful 22 percent reduction in the risk of death. Looking at the Kaplan-Meier curves, they separate early and the quizartinib curve, in blue, stays consistently above the placebo curve in green throughout follow-up, which extended to a median of about 39 months in both arms. Event rates were 50 percent with quizartinib versus 58 percent with placebo. This is the survival benefit that underlies the FDA approval of quizartinib in newly diagnosed FLT3-ITD AML.
keypoints: Median OS 31.9 months with quizartinib vs 15.1 months with placebo
22 percent reduction in risk of death, 16.8 month OS improvement
Curves separate early and remain separated through long-term follow-up
keypoint_voiceover: The headline numbers to remember. Median overall survival roughly doubled, 31.9 months versus 15.1 months. Hazard ratio 0.78, statistically significant at p equals 0.032. That translates to a 22 percent reduction in the risk of death, and the survival curves stay separated well beyond 3 years of follow-up, supporting a durable benefit rather than just an early effect.
